extracted.intended_audience: Researchers funded or co-funded by Wellcome; prospective authors and peer reviewers for Wellcome Open Research (and readers interested in open peer review).
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the Wellcome Open Research model of publishing-first with fully open, post-publication peer review and the standards used to select reviewers, declare conflicts, and promote trust and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open post-publication peer review model
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer-review takes place after an article has already been published, and all peer-review reports provided by reviewers are published online alongside the article so they are fully visible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This transparent, author-led model differs from traditional hidden peer review; publishing reports and reviewer details promotes constructive review, encourages reader engagement (comments on articles and reports), and allows readers to track article status in real time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author-led reviewer suggestions with editorial oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are allowed to suggest their own reviewers as part of an author-led peer review approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although authors suggest reviewers (they often know the field best), the editorial team carries out thorough checks on those suggestions to confirm qualifications and check conflicts of interest; this combination aims to improve understanding and trust while retaining editorial quality control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer academic qualifications and publication record
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should hold a PhD (or an MD) in a relevant field and have published at least 3 articles on the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editorial team checks that suggested reviewers meet these criteria to ensure they can provide current, in-depth and knowledgeable reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: No institutional or recent collaborative association with authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should not be associated with any of the authors of the paper, such as working at the same institution or publishing papers together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial checks include verifying institutional affiliations and recent co-authorship to avoid conflicts that could bias the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of other conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are asked to declare if there are any other conflicts of interest (e.g., friendships, funding) that might affect their impartiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All competing interests declared by reviewers are published alongside peer review reports so readers and future researchers have full information on possible influences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global spread of reviewers to reduce geographic bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Every article should obtain a global spread of reviewers to reduce country-to-country bias and gain an international perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial teams actively select reviewers from diverse countries to broaden viewpoints and reduce regional bias in evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case-by-case flexibility for reviewer eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer suitability checks are applied on a case-by-case basis depending on the subject area or reviewer country; some fields do not require PhDs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reviewer is widely published and is a current researcher in a field that commonly lacks PhDs, they can still be accepted despite formal qualifications not matching exactly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of competing interests (financial vs non-financial)
rubrics_metrics.description: Competing interests are considered across a wide range and are broken down into financial (e.g., software owned by the reviewer used in the article) and non-financial (e.g., having worked alongside the authors recently).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A fuller list of potential competing interests is maintained; transparency requires publishing these statements for both authors and reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation and correction of undeclared competing interests
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reader notifies the journal of an undeclared competing interest, the journal will investigate the allegation and, if necessary, highlight the issue on the peer review reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such investigations are rare but demonstrate accountability and help maintain trust when undeclared conflicts are discovered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish reviewer identities, affiliations and competing interest statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Names of reviewers, their affiliations and conflicts of interest are published alongside the article rather than kept anonymous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing this information together with the citable peer review report increases transparency and is believed to be beneficial for scholarly publishing and trust in the peer review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage public engagement and commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers are encouraged to contribute to the discussion between authors and reviewers, for example by leaving comments on the article and/or the peer-review reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open availability of reports and comments promotes community scrutiny, constructive discussion and additional perspectives beyond invited reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of ethical choices by authors when suggesting reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: The model relies on trust that authors will make ethical choices when suggesting potential reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because most researchers act as peer reviewers at some point, the journal expects them to understand what is required and to suggest appropriate, non-conflicted reviewers; editorial checks provide a safeguard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal: ensure reviews are current, in-depth and knowledgeable
rubrics_metrics.description: All checks are intended to ensure reviewers can provide a current, in-depth and knowledgeable review so articles get the best feedback possible and are indexed efficiently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection criteria (qualifications, publication record, lack of conflicts, international spread) are applied to maximize review quality and the utility of published work.
